title: The Surprisingly Serious Warm-Up
scene: You arrive early for a casual football game and do a surprisingly thorough warm-up. When your friends arrive, nobody has brought a ball, so the group decides to go for a run instead.
sceneJa: 気軽なサッカーの集まりに少し早く着き、一人でかなり真面目にウォーミングアップをする。ところが友人たちが到着すると誰もボールを持っておらず、代わりに全員で走ることになる。

chunks.ja: 小さなサッカーコートに着きました

chunks.en: a little earlier than everyone else,
chunks.ja: みんなより少し早く

chunks.en: so I decided to warm up
chunks.ja: そこでウォーミングアップをすることにしました
一人で

chunks.en: I started with a gentle jog
chunks.ja: 軽いジョギングから始めました
コートの周りを
そして妙に意識が高い気分になりました

chunks.en: for someone playing purely for fun.
chunks.ja: 完全に遊びでサッカーをする人間にしては
それからストレッチをして
短いダッシュを何本か行い
いくつかの動きもしました

chunks.en: I vaguely remembered from proper training sessions.
chunks.ja: ちゃんとした練習で見た記憶がうっすらある

chunks.en: By the time my friends arrived,
chunks.ja: 友人たちが到着するころには

chunks.en: I was already slightly out of breath
chunks.ja: すでに少し息が上がっていました
それでも真面目に準備したことには満足していて
自分が準備したことに
ところが
誰もボールを持ってきていませんでした

chunks.en: because each of us had assumed
chunks.ja: なぜなら全員が思い込んでいたからです
誰かほかの人が持ってくるだろうと

chunks.en: We spent the next ten minutes
chunks.ja: その後10分ほど過ごしました
バッグや車のトランクを確認しながら
徐々に希望を失いながら
やがて友人の一人が提案しました

chunks.en: that we simply go for a run instead,
chunks.ja: 代わりにただ走ればいいのではないかと
せっかくそこにいて
スポーツウェアも着ているのだから
みんな賛成しました
気楽な熱意をもって

chunks.en: of people who had not already
chunks.ja: まだすでに終えてはいない人たちらしい
不要なウォーミングアップを
説明しようかと考えました

chunks.en: that I had already done several sprints,
chunks.ja: 自分はすでに何本かダッシュしたことを
しかし、その情報は
場の空気を良くしないだろうと判断しました

chunks.en: So we went for a run,
chunks.ja: そこでみんなで走り始め

chunks.en: and I spent the first kilometre
chunks.ja: 最初の1キロを過ごしました
静かに考え直しながら
準備がいいことのメリットを
どうやら
準備というものは非常に役に立つようです
全員が準備しているなら
同じ活動のために

questions.question: Which boundary is most natural?
options: By the time my friends arrived / I was already slightly out of breath / but pleased with how seriously I had prepared
By the time / my friends arrived I was / already slightly out of breath but / pleased with how seriously I had prepared
By the time my / friends arrived I was already / slightly out of breath / but pleased with how seriously I had prepared
questions.explanation: ‘By the time my friends arrived’ sets the time frame, ‘I was already slightly out of breath’ gives the result, and the final chunk adds the speaker’s reaction.

questions.question: What does ‘each of us had assumed somebody else would bring one’ mean?
options: Everyone had agreed that one specific person would bring the ball
Each person expected another person to bring the ball, so nobody did
Nobody knew that a ball was needed
questions.explanation: Everyone independently relied on someone else to take responsibility, which is why the group ended up without a ball.

questions.question: Why is the final sentence funny?
options: It claims preparation is always unnecessary
It turns a simple mistake into a calm general rule about preparation
It suggests running is better than football
questions.explanation: The dry humour comes from treating a very ordinary coordination failure as if it revealed a formal principle about when preparation is useful.

speak: Start light and slightly proud, as if the warm-up feels sensible. At ‘Unfortunately,’ shift into mild confusion without becoming dramatic. Read ‘with steadily decreasing optimism’ very calmly. Give ‘would not improve the atmosphere’ a small pause before the final clause. Deliver the last sentence like a perfectly reasonable conclusion to a minor logistical failure.
review: Flow: early arrival → responsible preparation → preparation becomes excessive → missing ball reveals a coordination failure → backup plan creates extra effort → dry generalisation. Useful chunks: ‘by the time ...’, ‘assume someone else will ...’, and ‘provided ...’. Notice how the ending does not complain; it calmly converts the mistake into a conditional rule.
